mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a high-inflation regime where real rates fall.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when GDP deflator rises by more than 5% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, pushing wage inflation and input costs higher, which compresses profit margins and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation is below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a period of strong export demand.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of higher interest rates and inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: high inflation and tightening monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when the economy is in a deflationary shock.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and retail sales (RSAFS) above their 6-month averages signals a strengthening consumer demand environment, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a period of rising interest rates.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals a deepening labor market slack, which reduces wage pressures and supports corporate margins, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a period of rapidly rising commodity prices.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a housing market contraction, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a period of strong mortgage rate declines.
